claims.statement: The implemented scalar, O(2) matter and metric field equations (diagonal and t-x off-diagonal components) of the UET parent code follow from the Theory Card action UET-PARENT-ACTION-001.
claims.note: Mathematical consistency only; says nothing about whether nature follows this action.

claims.statement: epsilon is not an independent coupling of the parent action: in canonical variables xi_c and m_psi are epsilon-independent, lambda_psi ~ 1/epsilon and g_c ~ sqrt(epsilon), so epsilon = 0 is a degenerate point rather than a continuous GR limit.

Assuming ordinary matter couples minimally to the Jordan metric, the UET parent action maps onto the Damour-Esposito-Farese class with alpha0 = 0 and beta0 = -2 xi_c around psi0 = 0, so PPN gamma - 1 = 0 at that background.
claims.note: Mathematical mapping only; confrontation with binary-pulsar data is W6 (Test Card T001).

claims.statement: Binary-pulsar timing (ZFKSW22) excludes the UET non-minimal coupling interval that maps to the analysed DEF scalarization range, for a scalar light compared with the binary orbits; the parent action stays compatible for other xi_c.
claims.note: CONSTRAINT (not a prediction): xi_c in [2.0, 2.4] excluded for m_psi <= 2.5e-18 eV; L2 promotion approved by the author 2026-11-09.

claims.statement: In the layer-3 model, systems that disappear when their free-energy store F is exhausted at burn power P give steady abundance N* = b F/P (Little's law), replicator dynamics with fitness aR - P/F as an identity, and selection of the lowest R* = P/(a F) under a shared resource, without imposed payoffs.
claims.note: Mathematical consistency of the author's persistence-selection logic; no empirical confrontation yet.

claims.statement: The layer-3 abundance law N = b F/P, with stellar-model lifetimes and independently measured helium, predicts the horizontal-to-red-giant-branch star ratio in old globular clusters to within about 5 percent (R_pred = 1.467 +/- 0.023 vs R_obs = 1.39 +/- 0.03), a 2.05 sigma tension.
claims.note: CONSTRAINT, outcome INCONCLUSIVE by the preregistered rule (2 < z <= 3). Not a falsification and not a pass. L2 recording approved by the author 2026-11-09.

claims.statement: In the parent action, matter (the O(2) field) exchanges energy-momentum only with the response field, at the derived rate d^mu T_mu_nu = (1/2) eps h |chi|^2 d_nu phi on the matter shell; with h = 0 matter is separately conserved.
claims.note: Supports author point 2 mathematically. Calling the response field 'structure of space' is an interpretation.

claims.statement: The canonical UET potential has a true vacuum with psi0 != 0 when chi condenses (m2_chi < 0), and can have one with all masses positive when lam_chi is small (explicit example); then alpha0 != 0 and gamma_PPN != 1. A sufficient condition for psi0 = 0 is m2_chi > 0 and g_c^2 <= 2 lam_chi m2_psi.
claims.note: A falsification route for a future Test Card (Cassini); not yet confronted with data. With chi = ordinary matter (author 2026-11-10) the condensate branch m2_chi < 0 is excluded; only the metastable branch remains.

claims.statement: With chi identified as ordinary matter, the UET portal produces a composition-independent Yukawa force V = -G M m/r [1 + alpha exp(-r/lambda)] with alpha = g_c^2/(2 kappa m_chi^4) and lambda = 1/m_psi.
claims.note: Derived relation; not yet confronted with inverse-square-law, lunar or planetary data (planned Test Card T005).

claims.statement: With chi as ordinary matter, published fifth-force bounds limit the UET portal coupling: g_c < 5.1e-10 eV for m_psi <= 5.1e-3 eV (torsion balance) and g_c < 3.9e-15 eV at m_psi = 1.0e-15 eV (lunar laser ranging).
claims.note: CONSTRAINT, not a prediction; g_c remains free. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-10.

claims.statement: For a mode that is part of a closed Hamiltonian system with an ohmic environment, the open-system layer-2 laws emerge without being assumed: friction, burn power P = gamma x'^2, noise obeying the KMS/equipartition relation, heat flow from hot to cold, and exponential free-energy decay (P proportional to F).
claims.note: Supports author points 1, 4 and 8 at model level. Standard open-system physics (Caldeira-Leggett 1983); not yet tied to the parent-action fields.

claims.statement: With lifetimes derived from the layer-2 burn law, tau = integral dF/P(F), selection still favours the lowest R* = 1/(a tau), but tau = F0/P0 holds only for regulated burners; with two resources a mixed equilibrium exists and is Nash-stable against rare invaders.
claims.note: Supports author points 4 and 10 at model level. Ecology analogue: Tilman resource-ratio theory; not new physics by itself.

claims.statement: Each UET layer reduces to an established theory (layer 1: DEF scalar-tensor with a Yukawa portal; layer 2: Caldeira-Leggett open systems; layer 3: exactly the Tilman chemostat consumer-resource model). The only cross-layer effect found, a preferred-frame portal drag F = Gamma v q^2/(12 pi R), depends on three free parameters, so UET currently makes no numerical prediction that differs from standard physics.
claims.note: A negative result: the Theory Card's 'differences' field stays 'none yet', now with evidence.

claims.statement: The Sun's energy use (luminosity plus solar wind) is written into its gravitational parameter at the rate general relativity gives: predicted -8.76e-14 +/- 1.0e-14 per year against the MESSENGER measurement -6.13e-14 +/- 1.47e-14 (z = 1.48); no gravitational trace at all is disfavoured at 4.2 sigma.
claims.note: Supports author point 7 through standard physics; does not distinguish UET from GR. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-10.

claims.statement: Multimode laser rate equations are the layer-3 selection model term for term (a = stimulated-emission coefficient, tau = photon lifetime, F = 1, R = inversion); R* is the threshold inversion, one shared inversion gives single-mode lasing with gain clamping, and two inversion pools give two-mode coexistence.
claims.note: Shows author point 5 (selection by resource use, without learning) in a non-living physical system. Standard laser physics.

claims.statement: The trace that energy use leaves in the environment is the entropy production Sigma, which splits exactly into a readable record I(S:R) and a potential difference D (free energy T*D left in the environment); at long times D dominates, and the number of bits written is Sigma/ln 2, not Q/(kT ln 2).
claims.note: Author clarification 2026-11-10: the trace is a number or potential difference, not a new thing in the universe. Standard non-equilibrium physics.

claims.statement: Layer-3 resource selection with two essential resources predicts, from monoculture physiology alone, the dominance and coexistence regions of Tilman's (1977) diatom chemostats: predicted Si/P boundaries 86.9 and 6.2 against observed about 80 and 6; 2 of 3 ratio groups match fully and the Si/P = 38 group partly.
claims.note: Path-A test outside physics. Re-analysis with the same model Tilman used, not an independent experiment. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-10.

claims.statement: The burn-law lifetime of a passive burner (P ~ F^(7/2), Mestel cooling) plus the abundance law reproduces the slope of the SDSS white dwarf luminosity function: predicted 2/7 = 0.286 against observed 0.320 per magnitude (|log10| = 0.049).
claims.note: Path-A test in astronomy. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-10.

claims.statement: The abundance law N = b tau holds for the 238U-234U decay chain: the half-life inferred from secular-equilibrium abundances (245,670 +/- 260 yr) matches one measured without equilibrium (244,900 +/- 1340 yr), z = 0.56.
claims.note: Path-A test in nuclear physics. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-10.
